strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Building a dedicated BU pricing function to monetize EmployeeWorks through consumption (Assist) pricing on top of ServiceNow's AI-native tiers
strategy_updates.current_model: No public list prices. Since April 2026 ServiceNow sells Foundation, Advanced and Prime tiers that bundle Now Assist and Moveworks capabilities, with per-seat licences plus an annual pooled allowance of 'assists' (small/medium/large actions consume 25/50/150) and paid top-ups beyond the pool; legacy SKUs reached end of sale on 2026-07-01 (per partner Crossfuze's analysis of ServiceNow's commercial model overview). EmployeeWorks, launched in February 2026 on the Moveworks acquisition, has no published price.
posting_evidence: Director, Pricing and Packaging Strategy - Employee Experience Group (JB0076449), Mountain View, work persona 'Flexible or Remote'; released 2026-11-03; no pay range shown.
Sits in the EmployeeWorks Business Unit (department Product, function tag Marketing) and must keep EmployeeWorks pricing aligned with ServiceNow's central pricing team.

Explicitly owns the BU's consumption pricing strategy 'including the Assist rate card': proposing rate-card changes, working with Data Science and Engineering on usage metering, and analysing token spend to protect margins.
Go-to-market scope: SKU upsell and renewal 'glide paths', a pricing excellence hub for sales and renewals, and pricing across direct, partner, reseller and third-party channels.
Asks for 7+ years in pricing strategy, product monetization or financial analysis (SaaS or AI preferred), AI fluency, and comfort where 'playbooks are sparse'.

news.summary: Q3 2026 results: CFO says year-to-date AI consumption in production is up more than 13x year over year; the release highlights EmployeeWorks advances letting employees build AI agents with no code and a customer (INRY) that deployed EmployeeWorks in six weeks to replace its legacy portal.

strategy_updates.interpretation: ServiceNow appears to be pushing pricing ownership down into business units, starting with EmployeeWorks, its Moveworks-based employee 'front door' launched in February 2026 (inference from the BU-level requisition and its alignment mandate with central pricing). The role is framed around the Assist rate card and token-spend margins, which suggests the priority is to make agentic usage profitable as consumption grows (13x YoY per Q3) rather than to set seat prices. The no-code agent-building push in Q3 points to more variable, harder-to-forecast usage, so expect the job to be judged on rate-card design, overage and renewal mechanics, and gross margin per assist (inference). With no reporting line stated and a 'sparse playbooks' remit, the seat likely involves building the BU pricing practice largely from scratch.
open_questions: Who sets the Assist rate card today, the central pricing team or the BU, and what decision rights would this director have?
How is EmployeeWorks sold relative to the Foundation/Advanced/Prime tiers: included in assist pools, a separate SKU, or both?
What margin target per assist or per conversation is the BU working toward, and how are token costs from third-party models passed through?
strategy_updates.caveat: Tier and assist-pool details come from a ServiceNow partner's analysis, not ServiceNow's own price list; the 8-K gives no EmployeeWorks revenue or pricing data, and the reporting line is not stated.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Tightening SKU and catalog discipline in CPQ so new healthcare supply-chain software products and price changes launch cleanly
posting_evidence: Pricing Manager (Greenhouse req 1706), 'Office Location or Remote - USA'; first published 2026-08-11 and updated 2026-10-30; estimated salary $91,000-$121,000; up to 20% travel.

Sits in Product Management; the body calls the role 'Product Commercialization Manager', owning the SKU commercialization process from requirements through launch with Product, Deal Desk, Contract Ops and Finance.
Manages the full SKU lifecycle in Conga CPQ (formerly Apttus), leads catalog audits, governance and SKU rationalization, and maintains SOPs and a commercialization playbook.

Analyses sales, discounting and pricing trends to quantify revenue and margin impact, leads launch readiness for new products and pricing, and owns an AI/automation roadmap for commercialization; 5+ years in product ops, RevOps, deal desk or commercial program management required.
strategy_updates.interpretation: The posting points to a catalog and quote-to-cash clean-up rather than a pricing-strategy build: the emphasis on SKU rationalization, governance and CPQ hygiene suggests the product catalog has grown faster than its controls (inference). Timing may relate to the January 2026 agreement for Veritas Capital to take a majority stake, since new private-equity owners often push for price realization and discount control, but no source ties the role to that deal (inference, deal not read in full today). For a candidate this is a pricing-operations seat with influence on discount analytics, not ownership of price levels.
open_questions: Who owns price-level and packaging decisions at GHX, and does this role feed them or only implement them?
Is a CPQ re-platforming or catalog consolidation planned, and how many active SKUs are in scope?
What discount or price-realization targets, if any, has the new ownership set?
strategy_updates.caveat: Analysis rests on one operations-heavy posting; I found no GHX pricing news in the last three months and no public price list.
